AL.fieldCheck: Stand where a delivery driver leaves packages. Check that the camera shows the ground there as well as a visitor’s face.
AL.searchDescription: Considering a Google Nest Doorbell in Alabama? Check the porch view at midday and after dark, including a visitor’s face and packages left below the lens.

AZ.fieldCheck: Take a photo of the entry in late afternoon and bring it to the installation visit. Glare can be easier to see in that photo than on a floor plan.
AZ.searchDescription: Planning a Google Nest outdoor camera in Arizona? Compare shaded mounting positions and the effect of afternoon glare on your entry view.

AR.fieldCheck: Test the connection with the garage door closed. Mark an outlet and a mounting point before deciding whether the camera belongs on the garage or on the house.

CA.fieldCheck: If you already own cameras, list the models before the appointment. Ask which can stay in place and which require a new mount, power supply or app.

CO.fieldCheck: Choose a mounting height you can reach from a cleared path and check that a storm door can swing past the camera.
CO.searchDescription: Planning a Google Nest Doorbell installation in Colorado? Compare battery access, snow clearance and the swing of a storm door before choosing the mount.

CT.fieldCheck: Show the installer the indoor chime before the old button comes off. Ask to hear it ring and check the phone notification before the visit ends.

DE.fieldCheck: At the end of the visit, test an alert on the phone you take when you travel and show a local contact how to report an equipment problem.
DE.searchDescription: Planning ADT monitoring for a second home in Delaware? Test remote alerts, choose a local contact and plan who can meet an installer.

FL.fieldCheck: Have the installer show where exterior wiring enters the house. Keep a photo of the finished mount with the model number and service contact.
FL.searchDescription: Considering a Google Nest outdoor camera in Florida? Plan a sheltered mount, cable entry and weather protection before booking installation.

GA.fieldCheck: Put a box where deliveries usually land and open the front door. Check whether the box stays in frame in both positions.

ID.fieldCheck: Give the installer the service address and note any private road, detached entrance or gate that affects access to the property.

IL.fieldCheck: Bring the building’s mounting guidelines to the visit. Ask to see the proposed view with your apartment door and the neighboring door both closed.
IL.searchDescription: Considering a Google Nest Doorbell for an Illinois condo? Review building mounting rules and check what the camera sees from your shared hallway.

IN.fieldCheck: Trace your route from the car into the house. Check whether the alarm’s entry delay gives you time to disarm it from the door you normally use.

IA.fieldCheck: Mark two distances along the drive. Review a test image from each before agreeing on the mounting position.

KS.fieldCheck: List the panel, cameras and router separately. Have the installer explain which of those devices still works if the house loses power.

KY.fieldCheck: Have someone walk toward the house from both ends of the slope while you watch on the phone. Look for a face, not just the top of a head.

LA.fieldCheck: Check the proposed mount under the eave and look for a nearby gutter outlet. Ask how the finished cable will shed water.
LA.searchDescription: Compare outdoor camera mounting options for a Louisiana home. Ask how a Google Nest camera would be sheltered and where the installer would seal the cable.

MD.fieldCheck: Test the camera with a package on the bottom step. If the steps turn, check the approach from the sidewalk as well.

MA.fieldCheck: Show the installer any old keypad and door contacts. Label the doors before testing so you can tell which alerts belong to which entrance.

MI.fieldCheck: Plan the charging route before mounting the camera. Check whether you can remove the battery without taking the bracket off the wall.

MN.fieldCheck: Check how the doorbell comes off its bracket. If you wear gloves outside, try the release before choosing the final height.

MS.fieldCheck: Walk past the camera with the porch light on and off. Review a saved clip in each setting to see what a moving visitor looks like.

MO.fieldCheck: Give the basement door a name that differs from the upstairs back door, then check that the same name appears on the panel and phone.

NE.fieldCheck: Test the proposed location inside the closed building as well as outside it. Keep the test results with the estimate for any additional network equipment.

NV.fieldCheck: Compare the shade at the proposed spot in the morning and afternoon. Make sure the protected location still shows the approach to the door.
NV.searchDescription: Considering a Google Nest outdoor camera in Nevada? Compare shaded and sunny locations, then check the model’s rated temperature range.

NH.fieldCheck: Practice changing the call list before you leave for the season. Confirm that the local contact knows which entrance a technician should use.

NJ.fieldCheck: Test the camera feed using cellular data before leaving the house. This shows the view you will actually have when you are away from the home network.

NM.fieldCheck: Ask the installer to mark the proposed cable entry before drilling. Photograph the wall finish and agree on where the wire will be visible.

NY.fieldCheck: Check the building’s visitor-entry system with the installer. Decide whether you need an alert at your apartment door, the common entrance or both.

NC.fieldCheck: Walk from the driveway through the carport to the house. Mark the point where a visitor would leave the front camera’s view.

OH.fieldCheck: Test both garage entrances separately and ask the installer to use different names for them in the app.

OK.fieldCheck: Before the technician leaves, ask for a supervised backup test and a demonstration of the notification that tells you the primary connection is back.
OK.searchDescription: Considering ADT monitoring in Oklahoma? Plan an installation check for cellular alarm backup, camera recording and phone alerts during an outage.

OR.fieldCheck: Stand under the eave facing the street while someone checks the preview. Repeat from the steps so you can see how faces look as people move between light and shade.
OR.searchDescription: Planning a Google Nest Doorbell under a deep eave in Oregon? Test how a visitor appears between the shaded porch and bright street before installation.

PA.fieldCheck: Identify the indoor end of a proposed cable run as well as the exterior mount. Check what trim or finish will be affected on each side.

RI.fieldCheck: Ask the installer to point out each exposed connector. Keep the model’s cleaning instructions where you can find them before working on the lens.

SC.fieldCheck: Test the screen in the frame after dark as well as during daylight. Turn the porch light on to check for glare.
SC.searchDescription: Could a Google Nest Doorbell see through your screened porch in South Carolina? Compare the two door positions and test for glare after dark.

TN.fieldCheck: Walk through the front entry and lower landing separately. Check that you can tell from the notification which level someone entered.

TX.fieldCheck: Measure the distance along the actual cable route, including turns. Check day and night views from the gate and from a location nearer the house.
TX.searchDescription: Planning a Google Nest outdoor camera for a Texas driveway or gate? Measure the route to power and Wi-Fi and compare views at both mounting points.

UT.fieldCheck: Check whether the exterior basement door is visible from the upper entrance and whether the person opening it can reach the keypad in time.

VA.fieldCheck: Set a package against the wall and another on the lowest step. Look at each in the app with the exterior door both open and closed.

WA.fieldCheck: Check where water runs off the roof above the camera. Ask for a position you can reach to clean the lens between service visits.
WA.searchDescription: Planning a Google Nest camera at a Washington entry? Check roof runoff, lens cleaning access and the view from a sheltered mount.

WV.fieldCheck: Walk up toward the camera and then down from the opposite direction. Save one frame from each test to compare the mounting angles.

WI.fieldCheck: Open the storm door fully and set a box where deliveries land. Check that the hinge, frame and door sweep leave the view unobstructed.

DC.fieldCheck: Walk both stairways from the sidewalk. Check which doorway the main camera actually shows before deciding whether a second view is worth adding.
DC.searchDescription: Plan a home security installation in Washington, DC. Compare the view of upper and lower rowhouse entrances from the sidewalk before adding a second camera.
